court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: Integrated Finance Company vs M/S. Ravishankar Industries

parties.respondent_defendant: M/s. Ravishankar Industries Private Ltd., Respondent(s)

facts_of_case: This Criminal Appeal is filed against the judgment passed in CCNo.6199 of 1998, dated 20.07.2005 by the learned XVII Metropolitan Magistrate, Saidapet, Chennai.

legal_principles.principle: When a subsequent agreement has been entered into, the majority of the cheques which are supposed to be issued in respect of the original agreements cannot still be filled up and presented by the complainant organization.
legal_principles.held: The trial court held that when a subsequent agreement has been entered into, the majority of the cheques which are supposed to be issued in respect of the original agreements cannot still be filled up and presented by the complainant organization.

legal_principles.principle: The complainant has failed to prove that there existed a legally enforceable liability when the entire case is in doubt.
legal_principles.held: The trial court found that when the entire case is in doubt as to for which agreement the cheque has been issued and whether there exists a liability, etc., it was unsafe for the court to convict the accused and gave the benefit of the doubt and acquitted the accused.

legal_principles.principle: The power agent is not entitled to bring forth the case on behalf of the company if the resolution empowering them is faulty.
legal_principles.held: The trial court held that when the power agent is empowered only by such a faulty resolution, the concerned individual is also not entitled to bring forth the case on behalf of the company.

keywords: High Court of Judicature at Madras
use_for_drafting: advising on criminal proceedings for cheque dishonour
